# Lisbon 4-Day Trip Overview

A relaxed, museum-friendly Lisbon plan for **2025-09-10 to 2025-09-13** with **€900 total budget excluding flights**. I’ve kept each day walkable, food-focused, and balanced with at least one low-cost activity.

## Day-by-Day Lisbon Itinerary

| Day | Focus | Main Stops | Low-Cost Activity | Pace | Est. Spend |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Wed, Sep 10 | Historic center + first impressions | Baixa, Rossio, Chiado, Carmo area | Walk the viewpoints and old streets | **3/5** | **€185** |
| Thu, Sep 11 | Museums + riverside | Calouste Gulbenkian Museum, Parque Eduardo VII, riverside walk | Free park stroll and riverside promenade | **4/5** | **€230** |
| Fri, Sep 12 | Alfama + local food | Castelo area, Sé, Alfama lanes, Fado neighborhood | Self-guided Alfama walk | **3/5** | **€215** |
| Sat, Sep 13 | Belém + departure day | Belém Tower area, Jerónimos exterior, riverfront | Free monument exteriors and gardens | **2/5** | **€170** |

## Visual Itinerary Summary

### Day 1: Baixa, Chiado, and sunset viewpoints
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/building.svg
- Morning: Arrive, settle in, then explore **Baixa** and **Rossio** on foot.
- Afternoon: Visit **Carmo Convent** area and browse **Chiado** cafés and bookshops.
- Food: Try a classic **pastel de nata** and a simple bica coffee.
- Pace rating: **3/5** — easy walking, light first-day schedule.

### Day 2: Museums and green spaces
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/book.svg
- Morning: Spend time at the **Calouste Gulbenkian Museum** for a strong art and design stop.
- Afternoon: Walk through **Parque Eduardo VII** and continue toward the river.
- Food: Choose a budget lunch in a local tascas-style spot.
- Pace rating: **4/5** — museum-rich with moderate walking.

### Day 3: Alfama, history, and local flavors
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/geo-alt.svg
- Morning: Explore **Alfama** on foot with stops near **Sé Cathedral** and the castle area.
- Afternoon: Wander the narrow lanes, tiled facades, and small viewpoints.
- Food: Have grilled fish or a traditional **bacalhau** dish.
- Pace rating: **3/5** — scenic but hilly, best at a steady pace.

### Day 4: Belém and riverfront finale
Media: Icon=https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/bootstrap-icons@1.11.3/icons/water.svg
- Morning: Head to **Belém** for the riverside monuments and gardens.
- Afternoon: Enjoy a final relaxed walk along the Tagus and pick up souvenirs.
- Food: End with a **pastel de Belém** and lunch by the river.
- Pace rating: **2/5** — light day, good for departure timing.

## Budget Breakdown Chart

| Category | Planned Budget | Share |
|---|---:|---:|
| Accommodation | €360 | 40% |
| Food & drinks | €220 | 24% |
| Museums & entry fees | €110 | 12% |
| Local transport | €60 | 7% |
| Activities & experiences | €90 | 10% |
| Buffer / extras | €60 | 7% |
| Total | **€900** | **100%** |

### Budget Notes
- Lisbon can be very manageable if you mix **paid museums** with **free walking days**.
- Your budget leaves room for a few nicer meals without feeling rushed.
- Using trams/metro selectively helps keep transport costs low while preserving walking time.
